title: 3D & Blender
grandGoal: Become a 3D generalist who can carry an idea alone from blank scene to finished render or shot — modelling, UVs, texturing, shading, lighting, rigging, animation, FX and compositing.
note: Built for Blender 4.2 LTS and newer. Tiers are roughly 6-10 weeks each at 8-12 h/week, but the tree unlocks on skill, not on dates.

nodes.title: Interface & Navigation
nodes.unlocks: You can move around a scene and manipulate objects without hunting for buttons.
study: Viewport navigation: orbit, pan, zoom, numpad views, walk/fly mode
Editors, areas, workspaces — and how to split and join them
Outliner and Collections: naming, nesting, visibility vs. render visibility
Transforms G/R/S with axis locking, and what Object Origin actually is
Snapping, pivot points, and the 3D cursor
Saving: .blend files, incremental saves, Pack Resources, Append vs. Link
nodes.challenge: Rebuild a simple still life (3-5 primitives) matching a reference photo's rough proportions and camera angle. No modelling tools yet — position, rotation and scale only.
nodes.proof: A screenshot from the camera view next to the reference.

nodes.title: Box & Hard-Surface Modelling
nodes.unlocks: You can model a man-made object from reference with clean, deliberate geometry.
study: Edit Mode: vertex / edge / face selection, select linked, loops and rings
Core tools: Extrude, Inset, Bevel, Loop Cut, Knife, Bridge Edge Loops
Modifier stack: Mirror, Array, Solidify, Subdivision Surface, Boolean
Non-destructive thinking — why the stack beats baking changes in early
Support loops and how Subdivision Surface reacts to edge density
Reference setup: background images, real-world scale, unit settings
nodes.challenge: Model a hard-surface prop from a reference photo — a lantern, a camera, a mechanical keyboard. Mirror and Array must do work you did not do by hand.
nodes.proof: Wireframe screenshot plus a clay render.

nodes.title: Topology & Retopo
nodes.unlocks: You can judge whether a mesh will deform and subdivide well, and fix it when it won't.
study: Quads, tris, n-gons — where each is fine and where each bites
Edge flow: following form, and loops around eyes, mouths and joints
Poles (3, 5 and 6-point) and how to move them somewhere harmless
Manual retopology with the Shrinkwrap modifier and Poly Build
Common cleanup: Merge by Distance, Recalculate Normals, non-manifold hunting
Shading artefacts: Auto Smooth, custom split normals, Weighted Normal
nodes.challenge: Take a dense or messy mesh (a sculpt or a scan) and retopologise it to under 5k quads with clean loops around the main forms.
nodes.proof: Before/after wireframes and a smooth-shaded turntable.

nodes.title: Sculpting & Organic Form
nodes.unlocks: You can build organic shapes by feel instead of by vertex.
study: Sculpt mode brushes: Draw, Clay Strips, Grab, Crease, Smooth, Inflate
Dyntopo vs. Multiresolution vs. Voxel Remesh — when each is the right tool
Blocking with basic forms, then refining — silhouette first, detail last
Masking, Face Sets, Hide/Show for isolating what you are working on
Anatomy fundamentals: primary, secondary and tertiary forms
Baking sculpt detail down to a low-poly normal map
nodes.challenge: Sculpt a creature or character bust from a blockout, then retopologise it and bake the detail into a normal map.
nodes.proof: Sculpt turntable plus the baked low-poly beside it.

nodes.title: UV Unwrapping
nodes.unlocks: You can flatten a model so textures land on it without stretching.
study: What UV space actually is, and why 0-1 matters
Marking seams — hiding them where the eye won't follow
Unwrap, Smart UV Project, Follow Active Quads, Project From View
Reading the checker/stretch overlay to spot distortion
Packing, margins and consistent texel density across objects
Multiple UV maps, and when a second set earns its keep
nodes.challenge: Unwrap your hard-surface prop so a checker texture reads evenly everywhere, with no visible seam on a camera-facing surface.
nodes.proof: UV layout screenshot plus the model with a checker applied.

nodes.title: Texturing & PBR Maps
nodes.unlocks: You can author textures that describe a real material, not just a colour.
study: The PBR map set: Base Colour, Roughness, Metallic, Normal, Height, AO
What roughness actually communicates — wear, dust, fingerprints, polish
Texture painting in Blender: brushes, stencils, masks, layers via nodes
Baking: AO, normal, curvature — high-poly to low-poly cage setup
Trim sheets and tiling textures, and why they save enormous time
Texel density, texture resolution, and when 4K is a waste
nodes.challenge: Texture your prop as a used object with a believable story — where has it been gripped, scratched, dirtied?
nodes.proof: Flat map sheet plus a close render showing the wear.

nodes.title: Shader Editor Basics
nodes.unlocks: You can build a material from nodes rather than tweaking sliders blindly.
study: Principled BSDF, input by input — what each one physically means
Node types: Texture, Colour, Vector, Converter, and the Mix nodes
Image Texture nodes, colour space (sRGB vs Non-Colour — the classic bug)
Texture coordinates and Mapping: UV, Generated, Object
Bump vs. Normal vs. Displacement
Material slots, and assigning several materials to one mesh
nodes.challenge: Build five materials from scratch with no downloaded textures: brushed metal, worn wood, rough ceramic, frosted glass, car paint.
nodes.proof: A single render of five spheres, each labelled.

nodes.title: Procedural Shading
nodes.unlocks: You can generate detail mathematically instead of painting every pixel.
study: Noise, Voronoi, Musgrave/Wave textures and their scale/detail inputs
ColorRamp as the workhorse for shaping any grayscale signal
Geometry and Object Info nodes: pointiness, random per island
Node Groups — packaging a material so it has clean exposed controls
Layering masks: how procedural dirt, edge wear and grime stack
Where procedural stops paying off and painted maps take over
nodes.challenge: Build one fully procedural material with exposed controls (a node group) that a stranger could re-use — no image textures at all.
nodes.proof: The node group with named inputs, plus three looks from the same group.

nodes.title: Lighting Fundamentals
nodes.unlocks: You can light a subject so its form reads clearly.
study: Light types: Point, Sun, Spot, Area — and what each is physically like
Three-point lighting: key, fill, rim, and what each one is for
Inverse-square falloff — why moving a light beats changing its power
Size equals softness: the single biggest control over mood
Colour temperature, and warm/cool contrast
HDRI environment lighting and world settings
nodes.challenge: Light one object three ways — dramatic, neutral product, soft overcast — changing only lights, never the model.
nodes.proof: Three renders side by side.

nodes.title: Render Engines & Optimisation
nodes.unlocks: You can get a clean render out in reasonable time and know why it took that long.
study: Cycles vs. EEVEE Next: what each is actually good at
Samples, adaptive sampling, and the denoisers (OptiX / OpenImageDenoise)
Light paths and bounces — the usual cause of both noise and slowness
Colour management: Filmic vs. AgX, View Transform, Look, Exposure
Render passes and why you should almost always output multi-layer EXR
Output settings: resolution, file formats, and rendering animation safely
nodes.challenge: Take a noisy 10-minute render and get it to equal or better quality in under 3 minutes. Write down every change and what it bought.
nodes.proof: Both renders, both times, and the list of changes.

nodes.title: Composition & Camera
nodes.unlocks: You can frame a shot that holds attention rather than merely showing the model.
study: Focal length and what it does to perceived depth and distortion
Depth of field: f-stop, focus object, and when shallow is a crutch
Composition: thirds, leading lines, negative space, silhouette reading
Value structure — squint until it's grayscale and check it still reads
Camera rigs, and animating a camera along a path
Turntables and the standard portfolio presentation formats
nodes.challenge: Present one finished asset as a portfolio piece: hero render, three-quarter view, wireframe, clay, and a turntable.
nodes.proof: The full presentation sheet.

nodes.title: Geometry Nodes Basics
nodes.unlocks: You can build geometry from rules instead of placing it by hand.
study: The fields system: what a field is, and Value vs. Field sockets
Distribute Points on Faces, Instance on Points — the scattering backbone
Attributes: named attributes, Capture Attribute, Store Named Attribute
Randomisation: Random Value, per-instance rotation and scale
Realize Instances, and why it matters before exporting
Simple modifier-style rigs with exposed inputs on the modifier panel
nodes.challenge: Build a scatter system that populates a surface with three asset variants, with controls for density, scale spread and rotation.
nodes.proof: The node tree plus two very different results from the same setup.

nodes.title: Procedural Systems
nodes.unlocks: You can ship a parametric asset that someone else can drive.
study: Curves in Geometry Nodes: Curve to Mesh, profiles, resampling
Repeat Zones and Simulation Zones (4.x) for iterative and stateful setups
Instancing at scale — memory behaviour and viewport performance
Building a node group with a clean, documented interface
Combining Geometry Nodes with shading via named attributes
Knowing when a procedural rig costs more than modelling it by hand
nodes.challenge: Build one fully parametric asset — a modular staircase, a tree, a city block — driven only by modifier inputs.
nodes.proof: Four wildly different outputs from the same node group.

nodes.title: Armatures & Weight Painting
nodes.unlocks: You can make a model deform properly when it moves.
study: Armatures, bones, roll, and the parent/child hierarchy
Bone layers/collections and naming conventions (.L / .R and symmetry)
Skinning: automatic weights, then fixing them by hand
Weight painting: brushes, normalisation, the 4-influence practical limit
Testing deformation with extreme poses before you trust a rig
Shape keys and corrective shapes for problem areas
nodes.challenge: Rig a simple character and prove it holds up — no candy-wrapper twists at shoulders, elbows or hips at full range.
nodes.proof: A pose test video hitting extreme angles.

nodes.title: Constraints & Control Rigs
nodes.unlocks: You can build a rig an animator can actually use.
study: Constraints: Copy Transforms, Child Of, Damped Track, Limit Rotation
IK vs. FK, and building an IK/FK switch
Custom bone shapes, colours and a readable control layout
Drivers: linking a control to several outputs with an expression
Rigify — using it, and reading its output to learn from it
Rig hygiene: locking unused channels, hiding deform bones
nodes.challenge: Build a control rig with IK/FK switching on the limbs and at least one driver-based control (a hand-open slider, say).
nodes.proof: A screen recording of the controls being driven.

nodes.title: Animation Principles
nodes.unlocks: You can make motion that reads as intentional rather than floaty.
study: Keyframes, the Dope Sheet, and the Graph Editor as the real workspace
Interpolation and easing — Bezier handles, and why linear looks robotic
Timing and spacing: the two things that actually sell weight
Anticipation, follow-through, overlapping action, arcs
Pose-to-pose vs. straight-ahead workflows
Onion skinning, playblasts, and reviewing at real speed
nodes.challenge: Animate a bouncing ball with squash, stretch and arcs, then the same ball as bowling-ball heavy — only timing and spacing change.
nodes.proof: Both animations plus the graph editor curves.

nodes.title: Character Performance
nodes.unlocks: You can make a character act, not just move.
study: Body mechanics: walk and run cycles, weight shift, contact poses
Silhouette and readable key poses
Facial animation with shape keys and driven controls
Lip sync basics and phoneme shapes
Acting choices — intention before motion
The Non-Linear Animation editor and reusing actions
nodes.challenge: Animate a 5-10 second acted shot: the character wants something, tries, and reacts to the outcome.
nodes.proof: The rendered shot plus a playblast of your blocking pass.

nodes.title: Physics & Simulation
nodes.unlocks: You can let the solver do work that would be miserable by hand.
study: Rigid bodies: active/passive, collision shapes, margins
Cloth: pressure, self-collision, and pinning with vertex groups
Particles: emitters vs. hair, and children
Force fields and how they combine
Baking caches — and why an unbaked sim will betray you at render time
Substeps and quality settings: the accuracy/time trade
nodes.challenge: Produce a controlled destruction or cloth shot that lands where you want — not merely wherever physics threw it.
nodes.proof: The rendered sim plus your cache settings.

nodes.title: Volumes & Advanced FX
nodes.unlocks: You can produce smoke, fire and atmosphere that supports a shot.
study: Mantaflow smoke and fire: domain resolution, adaptive domain, noise
Fluid simulation, and why it costs so much more than it looks
Volume shading: density, emission, anisotropy, and scattering
Atmospheric depth — god rays, haze, and using volume to sell scale
VDB import/export for interchange
Simulating small and scaling up, so iteration stays survivable
nodes.challenge: Create an atmospheric shot where volumetrics carry the mood — not decoration bolted on at the end.
nodes.proof: Final render plus one without the volumes, for comparison.

nodes.title: Compositing & Passes
nodes.unlocks: You can finish a render instead of shipping the raw output.
study: The Compositor: Render Layers, Viewer, and the backdrop
Render passes: Combined, Z, Cryptomatte, Mist, AO, Emission
Cryptomatte for isolating objects without re-rendering
Glare, bloom, lens distortion, chromatic aberration — used sparingly
Colour grading nodes and matching a target look
Multi-layer EXR round-trips, and denoising in comp rather than in render
nodes.challenge: Take one raw render and grade it into two clearly different moods using passes alone — no re-rendering.
nodes.proof: Raw plus both graded versions, and the node tree.

nodes.title: Shot Assembly & Delivery
nodes.unlocks: You can deliver a finished piece to spec, not just a pretty frame.
study: Video Sequencer: cuts, transitions, audio sync
Frame rates, resolutions and codecs — and which to master vs. deliver in
Render farms and command-line rendering for long jobs
Naming, versioning and archiving a project so it survives you
Portfolio and breakdown presentation — showing the work behind the shot
Getting and using critique without drowning in it
nodes.challenge: Deliver one complete 10-20 second piece: modelled, textured, lit, animated, composited, cut and exported to spec.
nodes.proof: The final video plus a breakdown showing each stage.
